extracted.intended_audience: students (advanced undergraduates / beginning graduate students) learning foundations of algebraic geometry; readers of Ravi Vakil's 'The Rising Sea'.
extracted.subtask_description: Reading/using a textbook section on schemes, sheaves, gluing, projective constructions and graded rings; contains definitions, examples, and exercises intended to teach scheme-theoretic foundations. Useful for learning how to construct and reason about schemes (Spec, Proj), open/closed subschemes, stalks, fibers, rank, and graded rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence between isomorphisms Spec A ↔ Spec A' and ring isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe a bijection between the isomorphisms Spec A → Spec A' and the ring isomorphisms A' → A. (Exercise 4.3.A: show that if an isomorphism π : Spec A → Spec A' induces an isomorphism π♯ : A' → A, then π = ρ.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hardest part: show equality on the level of points (surprisingly tricky). Then show equality as maps of topological spaces, and finally equality on structure sheaves using the distinguished base. May use later insights but avoid circular arguments. Struggling with this exercise is pedagogically useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of D(f) with Spec A_f
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a natural isomorphism (Spec A_f, O_{Spec A_f}) ≅ (D(f), O_{Spec A}|_{D(f)}): the Zariski topology on Spec A restricts to give the Zariski topology on Spec A_f, and the structure sheaf of Spec A restricts to the structure sheaf of Spec A_f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 4.3.B: show identification using distinguished open sets; note distinguished opens of Spec A_f are already distinguished opens in Spec A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open subscheme and affine open subscheme
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a scheme and U is any open subset, then (U, O_X|_U) is also a scheme; such (U, O_X|_U) is called an open subscheme of X. If U is affine as a scheme we call it an affine open subset (or affine open subscheme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: D(f) is an affine open subscheme of Spec A. Note: not every affine open subscheme of Spec A need be of the form D(f) (see cross-reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine opens form a basis of Zariski topology
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a scheme, then the affine open sets form a base for the Zariski topology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 4.3.D: show affine opens cover and form a basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disjoint union of schemes and (non)affineness of unions
rubrics_metrics.description: The disjoint union of schemes is the disjoint union of underlying sets with the expected topology and sheaf. The disjoint union of a finite number of affine schemes is affine; an infinite disjoint union of nonempty affine schemes is not affine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 4.3.E: (a) finite disjoint union affine (hint: Exercise 3.6.A). (b) infinite disjoint union non-affine (hint: affine schemes are quasicompact, Exercise 3.6.G(a); see Remark 3.6.6). The disjoint-union construction will be the coproduct in the category of schemes once morphisms are known (Exercise 7.3.K).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed subschemes can have many scheme structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Closed subsets of a scheme can carry many 'natural' scheme structures; e.g., if I is an ideal then Spec A/I endows the closed subset V(I) ⊂ Spec A with a scheme structure, but different ideals can have the same vanishing set (e.g., (x) and (x^2) in k[x]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This motivates distinguishing 'closed subset' vs 'closed subscheme' and will be treated in detail later (see cross-references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Schemes are locally ringed spaces; stalks are local rings
rubrics_metrics.description: A ringed space is locally ringed if its stalks are local rings. For Spec A, the stalk of O_{Spec A} at the point [p] is the local ring A_p. Thus schemes are locally ringed spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Exercise 4.1.F for the stalk computation. Maximal ideal of O_{X,p} denoted m_{X,p} and residue field κ(p) = O_{X,p}/m_{X,p}. Functions on an open U have values in κ(p); 'vanish at p' means value in κ(p) is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Values of functions and residue fields; localization commutes with quotient
rubrics_metrics.description: For a point [p] of an affine scheme Spec A, the residue field at [p] is A_p/pA_p ≅ K(A/p), i.e., the fraction field of A/p. Localization at p and quotient by p 'commute'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See diagram (4.3.7.1) demonstrating commutativity. Examples show residue fields need not be algebraically closed even if A is a finitely generated C-algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locus where a function vanishes is closed; invertibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For f a function on a locally ringed space X, the subset where f vanishes is closed. (b) The subset where the germ of f is invertible is open. (c) If a function on a locally ringed space vanishes nowhere then it is invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 4.3.F: hints: show locus where germ is invertible is open; in a locally ringed space the locus where a function has nonzero value is open, while locus where it has nonzero germ is closed (contrast Caution 2.7.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiber and rank of an O_X-module at a point
rubrics_metrics.description: For an O_X-module F on a scheme X, define the fiber at a point p ∈ X by F|_p := F_p ⊗_{O_{X,p}} κ(p). The fiber is a vector space over κ(p). The rank of F at p is dim_{κ(p)} F|_p and denoted rank_p F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: O_X|_p ≅ κ(p) and rank_p O_X = 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manifold definitions as locally modeled ringed spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: A (topological / differentiable / C^∞) real manifold is a ringed space (X, O_X) whose underlying topological space is Hausdorff and second countable, and each point has an open neighborhood isomorphic to an open ball in R^n equipped with the sheaf of continuous (resp. differentiable, smooth) real-valued functions. A complex manifold is defined likewise with C^n and holomorphic functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unadorned term 'manifold' often means smooth manifold. This is a clean ringed-space formulation of manifold notions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic Hartogs-type extendability: functions on punctured affine plane extend
rubrics_metrics.description: Any function on A^2_k ">{(0,0)}" extends over all of A^2_k; i.e., Γ(A^2  ackslash {0}, O) = k[x,y]. This is an algebraic analogue of Hartogs's Lemma: functions defined on the complement of a codimension ≥2 set extend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example worked out by covering U = D(x) ∪ D(y) and computing Γ(U, O) = k[x,y] via intersection Ax ∩ Ay = A. See 4.4.2 and cross-reference to Theorem 12.3.14 for general statements (normality needed in singular cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use global sections to detect affineness (counterexample technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (U, O_X|_U) ≅ (Spec A, O_{Spec A}), then A = Γ(U, O_X|_U). Thus to show U is not affine, compute Γ(U, O) and argue the corresponding Spec is not homeomorphic (e.g., prime ideal (x,y) issue in A^2  ackslash {0}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show A^2  ackslash {0} is not affine: Γ(U, O) computed as k[x,y], but then (x,y) would have to correspond to a point of U which it does not, contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing schemes along isomorphic open subschemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Given schemes X and Y and open subschemes U ⊂ X, V ⊂ Y with an isomorphism π: U ≅ V (compatibility of structure sheaves), one can glue X and Y along U ↔ V to obtain a new scheme W: topological quotient of disjoint union with glued open sets, and sheaves glued by Exercise 2.5.E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The glued object is a scheme because every point has an affine neighborhood. The construction generalizes to arbitrary (even infinite) collections with cocycle data (see 4.4.A).

rubrics_metrics.name: General gluing data and cocycle condition for schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Given schemes X_i, open subschemes X_{ij} ⊂ X_i and isomorphisms f_{ij}: X_{ij} → X_{ji} with f_{ii} = id and the cocycle condition f_{ik}|_{X_{ij} ∩ X_{ik}} = f_{jk} ◦ f_{ij}|_{X_{ij} ∩ X_{jk}}, there exists a unique (up to unique isomorphism) scheme X obtained by gluing the X_i along this data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 4.4.A: hints ask to describe X as a set, topology, and sheaf of sections; check uniqueness and existence by local descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructions by gluing: doubled origin, projective line, projective space
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete gluings: glue two copies of A^1 along D(t) via isomorphism t ↔ u to get the affine line with doubled origin (non-affine); glue via t ↔ 1/u to get P^1_k; glue n+1 copies of A^n to form P^n_k with explicit coordinate identifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 4.4.B, 4.4.C, 4.4.6, 4.4.9, 4.4.E: check rings of global sections to deduce non-affineness where appropriate; verify triple overlaps when building P^n; interpret closed points of P^n as [a0:...:an] modulo scalars when k algebraically closed (Exercise 4.4.F).

rubrics_metrics.name: P^1_k and P^n_k have only constant global functions; not affine for n>0
rubrics_metrics.description: Γ(P^1_k, O) = k, hence P^1_k is not affine. More generally Γ(P^n_k, O) ≅ k and P^n_k is not affine if n>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof method: compute global sections on two affine patches and show only constants survive (e.g., polynomials in t which are also polynomials in 1/t must be constants). Relate to holomorphic fact that only constants exist on CP^1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and basic properties of Z-graded rings and homogeneous ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: A Z-graded ring S = ⊕_{n∈Z} S_n has multiplication sending S_m × S_n → S_{m+n}. Elements of S_n are homogeneous of degree n. An ideal I is homogeneous (graded) if it is generated by homogeneous elements; equivalently it contains the degree-n pieces of its elements for each n. The set of homogeneous ideals is closed under sum, product, intersection, radical. A homogeneous ideal I is prime iff for homogeneous a,b with ab ∈ I then a ∈ I or b ∈ I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 4.5.F and 4.5.G develop these facts. Nonstandard convention later used: for the book, a 'graded ring' means Z_{0}≥0-graded ring (no negative degrees) unless otherwise stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrelevant ideal S+ and finitely generated graded rings over base A
rubrics_metrics.description: For a graded ring S (Z_{0}≥0-graded), S_+ := ⊕_{i>0} S_i is the irrelevant ideal. If S_+ is finitely generated as an ideal, S is a finitely generated graded ring over A = S_0. If S is generated over A by S_1 (degree 1 generators) we say S is generated in degree 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key examples: A[x_0,...,x_n] and A[x_0,...,x_n]/I where I is homogeneous; Exercise 4.5.G gives equivalences with Noetherianity and finite generation statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of graded rings preserves grading; taking degree-zero part
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is a multiplicative subset of a graded ring S then T^{-1}S has a natural Z-grading. For homogeneous f ∈ S_+, localization S_{(f)} (or (S_f)) is graded and one can consider the degree-zero piece ((S_f))_0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is preparatory to the Proj construction: for each homogeneous f ∈ S_+ one considers Spec(((S_f))_0) as an affine patch for Proj S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proj S is built from affine pieces Spec(((S_f))_0) for homogeneous f
rubrics_metrics.description: To construct Proj S, for each homogeneous f ∈ S_+ consider the graded ring (S_f) and take its degree-zero piece ((S_f))_0; the affine schemes Spec(((S_f))_0) will be the building blocks for Proj S (as with Spec for rings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach avoids making ad-hoc choices (unlike preliminary glued construction of P^n) by simultaneously considering all possible affine patches given by homogeneous elements. Further details follow after this section.
